title: Integrated Security & Compliance Operational Guide: RBAC, Audit Logging, Data Residency, SDLC, Incident Response, Evidence Workflows, and Risk Exceptions
author: Aisha Khan
content:
Overview

Purpose: This document consolidates Redwood Inference’s operational policies and procedures for role-based access control (RBAC) and authentication, audit logging, data residency and retention, secure SDLC requirements, incident response security procedures, compliance evidence collection workflows, and the process for documenting and approving risk exceptions. It is the canonical operational guide for engineering, SRE, and security teams.

Scope: Applies to all production and pre-production systems, engineering and platform teams, private deployment packages, and customer-facing controls.

Owner & Review Cadence
- Primary owner: Security (owner: Aisha Khan)
- Operational owners: Eng-SRE (alerts/runbooks), Eng-Infra (accounts/networking), Eng-Serving-Runtime (runtime-specific audit hooks)
- Review cadence: Annual full review + triggered reviews for major platform changes (model onboarding, new regions, new compliance requirements).

1) RBAC & Authentication

Summary:
Redwood uses a least-privilege RBAC model implemented across control plane services, infra provisioning, and telemetry access. Authentication is single-sign-on (SSO) via SAML/OIDC for employees and mutual TLS + API keys/short-lived tokens for services.

Standards & Requirements:
- Principle of least privilege for all roles. Default access: read-only to non-essential metadata.
- Role categories: admin, platform-operator, oncall, dev, readonly, auditor.
- Privilege escalation: must be time-bound and recorded (see Temporary Elevated Access below).
- Service-to-service auth: mTLS with automated certificate rotation (90-day TTL recommended).
- API keys: rotated every 90 days; ephemeral tokens (OAuth 2.0) recommended for automation.

RBAC Matrix (example):
| Resource Type | Admin | Platform-Operator | Oncall | Dev | Readonly | Auditor |
|---------------|-------|-------------------|--------|-----|----------|---------|
| Console       | rw    | rw                | r      | r   | r        | r       |
| Deployments   | rw    | rw                | r      | rw  | r        | r       |
| Billing       | rw    | r                 | -      | -   | -        | r       |
| Audit Logs    | r     | r                 | r      | -   | -        | rw      |

Procedures:
1. Onboarding: New employees are assigned a role template in HR -> Okta group -> automatically provisioned. Devs receive dev access; platform operators receive platform-operator.
2. Access Review: Quarterly access review by resource owners; automated report generation via audit pipeline.
3. Temporary Elevated Access: Submit request in access-requests queue with justification. Approver: team manager + security. TTL: 8 hours (extendable with re-approval). All temporary elevation events trigger an audit log entry with approver and justification.

2) Audit Logging

Summary:
Comprehensive audit logging is required across control plane actions, model serving control operations, data access events, and security-related configuration changes. Logs are immutable, replicated, and stored in a centralized log service with retention policies mapped to compliance tiers.

Logging Requirements:
- Events to log: auth events (login, token issuance, key rotation), RBAC changes, config changes, deploys, secret access events, customer data access, admin/privileged commands, and incident response actions.
- Minimum log fields: timestamp (UTC), actor (user/service), action, resource, request_id, correlation_id, outcome (success/failure), reason (if failure), ip, region.
- Tamper-evidence: logs write-once with HMAC-chain integrity checks for high-sensitivity streams.

Retention & Access:
- Standard operational logs: 365 days (hot), then 2 years cold.
- Security-sensitive logs (auth, RBAC changes, admin actions): 7 years (per regulatory requirements for enterprise customers).
- Access: auditors and security have rw for audit stores; access must be via approved tooling and recorded in audit logs.

Alerting & SLOs:
- Log delivery SLO: 99.9% of events available for query within 60 seconds.
- Missing log detection: automated monitors (daily digests + oncall alert for >5% missing events in 24h).

3) Data Residency & Retention

Summary:
Data residency controls define where customer data and telemetry may be stored and processed. Retention policies are applied by data class (PII, model input/outputs, telemetry, logs). Customers can require region-restricted deployments (VPC Private) with contractually enforced residency.

Data Classification (examples):
- PII: customer account details, billing identifiers.
- Model IO: prompts, completions, embeddings. Marked as customer-data unless explicitly opted out.
- Telemetry: metrics, traces, non-identifying usage.
- Audit logs: security and auth data.

Residency & Retention Table:
| Data Class | Default Residency | Retention (default) | Customer-configurable | Legal Hold Support |
|------------|-------------------|---------------------|-----------------------|--------------------|
| PII        | US/EU (by account) | 7 years             | Yes                   | Yes                |
| Model IO   | region of request  | 30 days             | Yes (customer-request) | Yes               |
| Telemetry  | multi-region      | 365 days            | No                    | No                 |
| Audit Logs | US/EU depending on agreement | 7 years | No            | Yes                |

Procedures:
1. Customer Residency Requests: Sales/Legal opens an onboarding ticket with compliance tags; Infra provisions region-specific clusters; Security validates encryption and networking (private gateways).
2. Data Deletion / Erasure: Provide API and DSAR template for account deletion. Deletion process: mark -> soft-delete (30 days) -> purge. Customer can request immediate purge with signed SLA.
3. Legal Holds: Legal team can request hold via the evidence portal; flagged data moves to hold tier and retention freezes.

4) Secure SDLC Requirements

Principles:
- Shift-left security: threat modeling, secure code reviews, and dependency scanning integrated into CI/CD.
- Build reproducible artifacts: signed builds and SBOMs for release artifacts.
- Secrets management: no secrets in code; use vault with short-lived credentials for CI jobs.

Mandatory Gates (pre-merge / pre-release):
- Static Application Security Testing (SAST) pass with 0 high-severity findings (or documented mitigation).
- Dependency vulnerability scan: no critical unpatched CVEs.
- Threat model update for public-facing or large-scope changes.
- Fuzzing / dynamic tests for serving runtime changes that touch memory/kernel paths.
- Signed release artifacts and SBOMs attached to release notes.

Ownership & Tooling:
- Dev teams own unit and integration tests; Security owns SAST/SCA pipelines and config.
- CI/CD: centralized pipelines in eng-infra with enforced secrets and artifact signing.

5) Incident Response (Security Procedures)

Overview:
Incident response follows a standard lifecycle: Detect -> Triage -> Contain -> Eradicate -> Recover -> Lessons Learned. This section focuses on security-specific controls (forensics, coordination, and compliance evidence collection).

Key Contacts:
- Incident Commander (IC): rotating oncall from Eng-SRE for availability incidents; Security IC from Security team for confirmed compromises.
- Pager escalation: incident playbooks list contact trees and communications templates.

Forensics & Evidence Preservation:
1. Immediately preserve relevant logs and snapshots (write-blocked copies) upon suspected compromise.
2. Tag and store evidence in the evidence repository with chain-of-custody metadata (who collected it, timestamp, hash).
3. Engage Legal when exfiltration of customer data is suspected.

Containment Steps (example):
1. Isolate affected nodes or services (network ACLs, instance termination in private clusters).
2. Rotate keys and credentials with blast-radius minimization.
3. Disable compromised accounts and trigger password/API key resets.

Communication & Reporting:
- Customer-facing incidents: follow the customer communication policy; legal and customer success coordinate messages.
- Regulatory reporting: PII breaches trigger legal assessment for required notifications (72-hour GDPR window when applicable).

Post-Incident:
- Conduct a postmortem within 7 days for SEV3+ incidents and within 30 days for lower-severity security events. Postmortems require a security review and action item tracking in the roadmap.

6) Compliance Evidence Workflows

Purpose:
Maintain an auditable trail of controls, artifacts, and evidence for audits (SOC2, ISO27001, customer attestations).

Evidence Types & Sources:
- Control evidence: RBAC access review reports, change control tickets, signed releases, SBOMs.
- Operational evidence: runbook execution logs, incident postmortems, retention proofs.
- Technical evidence: configuration snapshots, firewall rules, log retention proofs, certificate rotation records.

Workflow Steps:
1. Evidence Collection: automated collectors push artifacts to the evidence portal (immutable store). Where automation is not possible, teams upload documents to the evidence portal with a reviewer.
2. Review & Attestation: Control owners review and attest quarterly. Attestation is recorded with reviewer name and timestamp.
3. Audit Support: For external audits, Security generates an evidence package scoped to auditor requests, with an index file and chain-of-custody hashes.

Evidence Retention & Access:
- Evidence artifacts retained per control: default 7 years.
- Access: Restricted to Security, Audit, and assigned reviewers. Exported packages are time-limited and watermarked.

7) Risk Exceptions & Approval Process

Definition: A risk exception is a documented deviation from a security policy or control that is accepted by reviewers for a defined scope and period.

When to use: Temporary business-critical needs (e.g., third-party integration with legacy auth) that cannot meet standard controls immediately.

Approval Flow:
1. Submit exception request in the risk-exceptions tracker with description, affected scope, compensating controls, estimated duration, and business justification.
2. Security reviews request and issues risk rating (Low/Medium/High).
3. Approval matrix: Low — Security owner; Medium — Security + Eng manager; High — CISO + Legal + Exec sponsor.
4. Approved exceptions include a remediation plan and fixed review date (max 90 days for Medium, 30 days for High).

Compensating Controls Examples:
- Enhanced monitoring and three-times-daily log snapshots.
- Network isolation (VLAN/VPC restrictions) and strict ingress rules.
- Time-limited credentials and additional authentication factors.

Records & Auditability:
- All exceptions recorded in the evidence portal and included in quarterly compliance reports. Exception status tracked and surfaced in the security dashboard.

Appendices
A. Quick Checklist for New Production Service
- RBAC role template created and assigned.
- SSO/Service auth configured (mTLS or OAuth).
- Audit logging enabled and verified for all control plane actions.
- Retention classification documented and mapped to storage tier.
- CI/CD gates configured (SAST, SCA, signed artifacts).
- Runbooks added to incident playbook library.
- SBOMs attached to release.

B. Example CLI Commands & Templates
- Rotate API key (example):
  curl -X POST "https://controlplane.redwood.ai/api/v1/keys/rotate" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" -d '{"service":"ingest-worker"}'

- Access request template: title, justification, duration, approver, resources_affected, risk_mitigation.

C. Contact Matrix
- Security Pager: security-oncall@redwood.ai (PagerDuty)
- Incident Commander (Security): security-ic@redwood.ai
- Legal: legal@redwood.ai
- Customer Success Escalation: cs-escalation@redwood.ai
